description: A message to the chat from someone other than you (a Bot, another chat, a subagent's answer, a host), as the chat's host records the sender: placed where your messages are, at the right, but grey, with who it's from in a small line at the top of the bubble.
opens: A Bot, another chat or a subagent messages this chat over the mesh
A held message sent with its ↑ (HeldTurn)
Opening a chat whose host's sender store says a message is someone else's

A message from a Bot, another chat or a host sent to the open chat: appears as its agent is given it, as theirs from the start (the host says who it's from with it), placed as a message of yours sent from elsewhere is (UserTurn), mid-turn included. The phone shows it in the same place
Auto-fix, the chat's host following the pull request of its branch (Git.panel's Auto-fix), sends what needs fixing on it: from "Auto-fix" (a host's kind of sender, by its name)

parts.name: bubble
parts.shows: A sent-message bubble (right-aligned, 12px corners, attachments then markdown text), filled with the text colour at 7% (grey) instead of the accent; its text in the normal colour (not dimmed like a queued one). The hidden line the host puts at the head of the text for the agent ("A message from …, not from your user") is never shown; if the host says what to show of it (a held answer), that is shown instead of the full text. A chat a Bot's task's run started telling the Bot what it said: the bubble is only that chat's own words, never a line of the app's around them; what the task and run were and how the turn ended go in the from line, and the Bot's agent is told them in the hidden line. A task's run asking its Bot, handing it a failure, or telling it it finished (its script's ask or fallback, or the host once a run has failed): the bubble starts "An instance of the '<task>' task asks:" (or "… task failed", or "… task finished" for a run that ended with exit 0, told to its Bot for its information), then a two-column table of the run, one row each, a row left out when it isn't known: task (the task's id), run (the run's id), both in full as the Bot's task and task_run tools take them; start time; end time (both on the host's clock, with no time zone) and exit code (only once its script has exited); duration (so far, while it runs); version; command (what the run runs, in full: its interpreter and its script's path; left out for a task given its Bot as a turn). The script's own words and its form follow.

decisions.said: Where does the "Your task" copy text come from? I really don't like how it just appears in the main text area. … It can be less anal and just be "An instance of the '...' task (<id...>) failed" |start time|...| |end time|...| |duration|...| |version|...| |entrypoint|...| |script|...| |exit code|...| … It might be importatnt o preserve the run id and the taask id … In that case there is no need to interpsers ethem in parentheses in sentence. one
decisions.rule: Every app's message from a task's run to its Bot (an ask, or a failure handed over) starts with "An instance of the '<task>' task failed" (or "… asks:") and no ids in that sentence, then a table of the run: task id and run id first, in full, then start time, end time, duration, version, command and exit code, a row left out that isn't known; no parenthesised line of the app's in the message's text

decisions.said: Time zone isp robably overkill here
decisions.rule: Every app's table of a task's run gives its start and end times on the host's clock as "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS", with no time zone or UTC offset
Every app's table of a task's run has one command row, the full command the run runs (interpreter and script path), in place of separate entrypoint and script rows

parts.name: from line
parts.shows: At the top of the bubble, right-aligned, wrapping: "from <who>" at 0.85em and 60% opacity. <who> is: "<name>, a Bot" (or "a Bot, a Bot" without a name); "“<chat title>”" (or "a chat"); "subagent “<name>”" (or "a subagent"); a host's name (or "a host"); another kind by its name (or "another"). For anything but a host, " on <host>" follows when the sender's host is known, e.g. "from Ada, a Bot on lab-mac". When the sender names a chat (a Bot, a chat, a subagent: its session), the line is a link (underlined, link colour): it opens that chat on its host. A task's run's (a host sender naming a run: what a run sends a chat it starts, and its asks of its Bot) opens the run's Bot's chat on its Tasks page, at that run. A chat a task's run started, telling its Bot what it said (a subagent sender naming the run's Bot, task and run, and how its turn ended), adds " · <task> run" (a link: the run, on the Bot's Tasks page, its task's page under it, so Back goes to that task) and " · finished" (or "stopped", "failed"), each joined by " · ", e.g. "from subagent “Why the deploy failed” on lab-mac · Deploy site run · finished"; its name is a link to its chat. A task's own line in a chat its run started ("from Task “Deploy site”") and on its asks of its Bot is a link to the run.

actions.does: on who it's from: opens the chat it's from (a task's: its Bot's Tasks page at that run, its task's page under it)
on "<task> run": opens the run's Bot's chat on its Tasks page at that run, its task's page under it

parts.name: revert button
parts.shows: As a sent message's (UserTurn): fades in left of the bubble on hover.

phone.does: A long-press reveals the same controls
phone.why: No hover on touch; a long-press is Android's equivalent of the desktop's right-click

actions.does: Tentative revert of it and everything after it, but its words are NOT put in your composer; sending (even with nothing in the composer) makes the revert.

states.name: sender learned late
states.shows: A message first drawn as yours turns into this look in place once the host's sender store arrives and says it's someone else's.

decisions.rule: A message an agent outside the apps (baude-mcp's message_chat) sends a chat carries its name as the sender (as_agent) and is drawn as from it, not as the user's, as Meta's are.

decisions.said: * Philosophy: I have a deployment tak that fallsback to a oneshot agent when teh deploy fails. But the oneshot agent spawned outside of the bot which is not ideal, and did not keep in touch with the bot either.
decisions.rule: Every app's from line links to the chat a message is from, so a Bot told what a task's agent said can open that agent's chat, and that agent's chat can open the run that started it

decisions.said: Dont really like how the oneshot messages mix. agent text and template text
decisions.rule: Every app shows a message a chat a task's run started sends its Bot as only that chat's own words. The context (the chat, a link; the task's run, a link; finished, stopped or failed) is in the from line, and the Bot's agent gets it in the sender's hidden line (baude-sender), not as text of the message. That chat's own first message shows the task's prompt as it is, from "Task “<name>”"
